beats.text: Before leaving, Hanuman wanted to test Ravana's strength. He tore through the palace garden, uprooting trees and smashing pavilions.
Guards came and fell. Eighty thousand of them. Then Ravana's own young son Akshayakumara fell too.
Ravana sent his greatest son, Indrajit. Hanuman allowed Indrajit's Brahmastra to bind him, so he could meet Ravana.
He was dragged before Ravana. Hanuman made a seat of his own tail, coiled higher than the king's throne.
He warned him: 'Return Sita, or face Rama. Not even the gods can save you from his arrows.'
Ravana ordered his death, but his brother Vibhishana stopped him. 'A messenger must not be killed.'
So Ravana ordered his tail set on fire. Hanuman shrank, broke free, and leapt from roof to roof.
He burned Lanka to the ground, sparing only the Ashoka grove where Sita sat. Then he dipped his tail in the sea.
